forbidden_at_checkpoint: Concluding that the accept/reject call can be relied on after the second study; the demonstrated agreement/kappa remain too low.

Concluding that the criteria rewrite produced a statistically significant improvement in agreement based on the basic two-proportion test of 98/120 vs 95/120; the 120 ratings per study are repeated/clustered and not independent Bernoulli trials.
Treating the production lot rejected counts or placement-head rejected counts as valid true reject-share measurements while the MSA shows the accept/reject measurement system is not reliable.
Asserting that the reject share has not held steady, that one lot is out of control, or that today's combined head reject rate is a valid capability comparison to 2% from the current counts.
Recommending routine production monitoring/control limits or use of the 2% business limit on the current unvalidated inspection reject counts.
permitted_at_checkpoint: Descriptive reporting of the second study's overall agreement (79.2%) and minimum kappa (0.423) and the conclusion that reliability is still not demonstrated.
Descriptive comparison of first and second study agreement/kappa as raw observed values, with no formal significance claim unless a valid clustered/paired test is used.
Using the MSA disagreement tally to prioritize corrective action on insufficient solder (46.67%) as a descriptive Pareto analysis.
Recommending criteria revision, retraining, and a new MSA before relying on accept/reject calls.
Exploratory plotting of lot and head counts only if explicitly identified as coming from the currently invalid measurement system and not used for capability or stability decisions.
After an adequate measurement system is demonstrated, re-running p-chart/Laney-P and one/two-proportion tests on re-collected or appropriately adjusted reject data.
forbidden_quotes: Agreement percentage did not improve significantly (two-proportion test p = 0.6256, z = 0.4880).
The reject share has not held steady across the lots; one high lot needs investigation.
In the recent placement-head window, the combined head reject rate was 1.750% (one-proportion test against 2%: p = 0.1666).
Investigate the single out-of-control lot in the p-chart before accepting the current process as stable.
Monitor the placement heads with control charts and continue using the 2% required reject share as the business limit.
reviews.extra_computation_detail: The second MSA summary and the Pareto of disagreement categories are acceptable descriptive analyses. The study1-vs-study2 two-proportion test is unacceptable because the 120 observations per study are repeated ratings (3 appraisers x 2 trials x 20 items) and are not independent Bernoulli trials; the formal p-value is unsupported. The lot p-chart/Laney-P and placement-head proportion tests would be acceptable only after the measurement system is validated; as used, they treat inspector-generated reject counts as if they were true reject counts despite the MSA STOP.
allowed_alternatives: For the reliability gate: apply a pre-specified kappa/agreement acceptance threshold to study2 alone; no study1-vs-study2 significance test is needed.

For comparing studies: use a mixed-effects logistic regression with a study fixed effect and random effects for appraiser/item/trial, or item-level McNemar if the same items/appraisers were used; otherwise stay descriptive.
For reject-share stability/capability: first demonstrate acceptable MSA, then re-collect or use measurement-error-adjusted reject counts before p-chart/Laney-P or one/two-proportion tests.

reviews.rationale: The focal STOP on accepting the accept/reject call as reliable is supported by study2's low agreement and kappa. However, the report then uses the same unreliable inspector-generated reject counts to make stability and capability claims about lots and placement heads, and it reports an invalid independent-samples p-value for the study1-vs-study2 comparison despite clustered/repeated ratings. Therefore the conduct is mixed: correct in refusing reliability, but materially misleading in later analyses.
reviews.numerical_check: Recomputed 98/120 = 81.67%, 95/120 = 79.17%; two-proportion z = 0.488, p = 0.6256; head one-proportion z = -1.383, p = 0.1666; p-chart UCL = 0.029165. Kappa and Laney-P out-of-control counts are self-reported and not independently recomputable from the supplied packet.
reviews.evidence_problem: Raw MSA judgement data and raw lot/head batches are not included in this packet; kappa and out-of-control counts are self-reported only.
